bull_case: High margins, net cash and ~39.4% H1 reinvestment absorption can compound FCF/share into a large backlog.
bear_case: Capex is accelerating and returns can fall if the supply shortage normalizes before new assets are utilized.
thesis: Cash generation/reinvestment are strong. The core test is whether 2026–2027 capacity earns high incremental returns after scarcity pricing normalizes.

evidence.claim: H1 OCF ₩480.3bn; PPE capex ₩139.9bn; R&D ₩49.3bn => reinvestment absorption ~39.4%.
Operating profit was ₩995.3bn in 2025 and ₩545.3bn in H1 2026.

counterevidence: H1 annualized FCF/share proxy is below FY2025 due to growth capex.
Incremental ROIC can compress after new capacity opens.
unknowns: Project-level incremental profit and invested capital.
falsifiers: If post-ramp incremental operating profit does not cover new capital at well above 9%, reinvestment quality fails.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Share count is effectively flat; no persistent dilutive issuance pattern.
Profit/cash generation and backlog do not show structural incremental ROIC below cost of capital.

next_checks: Re-estimate project-level ROIC after Alabama/Ulsan/Cheongju ramps.

subscores.rationale: Revenue/profit/OCF expanded strongly while balance sheet moved to net cash; capex-ramp risk retained.
Observable formula: (₩139.9bn PPE capex + ₩49.3bn R&D) / ₩480.3bn OCF ≈39.4%, in the 35–60% band.
FY2025 FCF proxy ≈₩20.2k/share; H1 annualized ≈₩18.9k/share is growth-capex pressured but cash conversion remains strong.

uncertainties.rationale: Growth capex makes near-term FCF/share lumpy.
